verdicts.title: Connecting the Built-in Multi-Star Guider is a silent no-op: no connection, no error, no UI change
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced on a fresh v-sequencer-run profile with the camera+mount+focuser+filterwheel simulators connected. Equipment > Discovery > GUIDERS > Built-in Multi-Star Guider > Connect does NOT fail silently: a modal 'Connection help' dialog appears, headed 'The connection didn't complete', body 'The guide camera connection didn't complete and we couldn't pin down the exact cause', with four numbered remediation steps, an expandable 'Technical details' section carrying the raw driver message, and Close / 'Retry connection' actions (evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsr-10.png). Timing measured: the first attempt surfaced the dialog ~13s after the click (log 'Connecting to Guider device' at 16:03:40, dialog present by 16:03:53 - i.e. the native connect timeout). I then closed the dialog, confirmed via tree that it was gone, clicked Connect again, and the dialog was back within 4s; repeated twice. The log evidence the finding cites is accurate ('Connecting to Guider device' + 'Registered device from ID' and no success/error line) but the inference from it is wrong - the failure is reported through the UI, not the log. The row correctly stays on 'Connect' and the status bar correctly stays 'Guider Disconnected' because the connect really did fail (the built-in multi-star guider needs a guide camera; none is assigned). The System Health drop is also not silent: the STATUS card renders '75 - Good' with a '1 issue' chip and enumerates the issue. Most plausible explanation for the original report: the tree was sampled at t+15s, right around the first-attempt timeout, and never re-read.

verdicts.title: Quick-Start Wizard opens as an empty black panel with no content, no controls and no accessibility nodes
verdicts.reasoning: Same entry point (Sequencer > Builder > toolbar wand icon, 4 sim devices connected, empty 'New Sequence' loaded) and the wizard renders completely. Within ~5s of the click the accessibility tree held 'Quick-Start Sequence Wizard / Step 1 of 5: Choose Your Target', the body 'Search for a target or enter coordinates manually.', three text fields (Target Name, Right Ascension, Declination) and both actions (Cancel, Next) - the direct opposite of the finding's load-bearing claim that 'the accessibility tree contained zero wizard nodes'. Screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsr-12.png shows it fully painted: title, subtitle, 5-segment step rail with segment 1 filled, search field, RA/Dec pair, Cancel/Next footer. I cancelled and reopened; it built identically the second time. If the original agent saw a black rectangle it was a one-off softpipe paint fault in their session, not a defect in the wizard - and the 'no semantics were ever built' claim is what makes the finding actively misleading, since it would send a fixer into _wizard_shell.dart looking for a bug that is not there.

verdicts.title: Captured frames are written to the DB with NO gain, offset, sensor temperature, mount pointing, focuser position or target link - although the FITS file it just wrote has all of them
verdicts.location_wrong: unit says 'screen:sequencer/sequencer_screen.dart'; the defect is in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/daos/images_dao.dart:657 (insertSequenceFrame) and its only production caller packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/sequence_executor/event_operations.dart:708. sequencer_screen.dart has nothing to do with capture persistence.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced from scratch on my own profile. Built Sequence > New Target > Take Exposures 4x3s LIGHT (node Filter empty, Gain/Offset left at 'profile' placeholders), ran it to completion against the sim camera/mount/focuser/filter wheel. Four FITS files landed in /tmp/ns-audit/v-sequencer-run/captures. FITS header of New Target_nofilter_0001.fits: GAIN=100, OFFSET=10, CCD-TEMP=20.0, XBINNING/YBINNING=1, SITELAT=30.0, SITELONG=82.0, RA=0.0, OBJCTRA='00 00 00.00', DEC=0.0, OBJCTDEC='+00 00 00.00', FOCUSPOS=25000, FOCTEMP=20.0, OBJECT='New Target'. The four matching captured_images rows: gain, offset, sensor_temp, cooler_power, mount_ra, mount_dec, mount_altitude, mount_azimuth, pier_side, focuser_position, focuser_temp and rotator_angle are ALL NULL, and target_id is NULL - while hfr (2.48-2.53), star_count (39), eccentricity, filter, exposure_duration (3.0), bin_x and session_id (1) were persisted. Identical to the reported row-for-row. Root cause read out of the source, and it splits in two, which matters for whoever fixes it: (a) sensor_temp, cooler_power, mount_ra/dec/altitude/azimuth, pier_side, focuser_position, focuser_temp and rotator_angle are not in insertSequenceFrame's INSERT column list at all - the sequencer path can never write them, no matter what the camera reported; (b) gain and offset ARE parameters and ARE passed, but they come from `attribution.gain/offset` (the producing ExposureNode's per-node override) rather than from the value the camera actually used, so a node left on the profile default writes NULL while the FITS card written microseconds earlier says 100/10. target_id is likewise resolved from the sequence tree and stays NULL because an ad-hoc Target node is not linked to a `targets` row (the targets table is empty after the run) - so the Session Report itself files the frames under 'Untargeted' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsr-18.png). P1 stands: dark-library matching keys on gain/offset/temp/binning, and analytics/project tracking read the DB, not the file.

verdicts.title: Four surfaces disagree about which filter a frame was taken through: filename says 'nofilter', DB says 'R', FITS header has no FILTER card, run stats say 'Unknown'
verdicts.location_wrong: unit says 'screen:sequencer/session_report_dialog.dart' - the dialog is only one of the five disagreeing readers and is not where any of it is decided. The writers are the Rust FITS/filename writer (no FILTER card, 'nofilter' token), event_operations.dart:~625 (DB filter = progress.currentFilter ?? filterWheelStateProvider.currentFilterName) and whatever builds sequence_runs.stats_json's targetBreakdown.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced with my own run (Target > Take Exposures 4x3s, node Filter field empty - 'No filters in profile' - and the sim wheel sitting on slot R). All five surfaces, verified independently: (1) files on disk are 'New Target_nofilter_0001.fits' .. '_0004.fits'; (2) sqlite captured_images.filter = 'R' for all four rows; (3) the FITS header of _0001 has 27 cards and no FILTER card at all (dumped byte-wise, not via the app); (4) sequence_runs.stats_json for run 1 = {"targetBreakdown":{"New Sequence":{"Unknown":{"captured":4,"rejected":0,"integrationSecs":12.0}}}} - bucket key 'Unknown'; (5) the Session Report's Targets table shows Filter 'R' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vsr-18.png). Exactly the reported four-way (five-way) split. Two things the finding did not mention and a fixer should know: the same targetBreakdown keys the TARGET as 'New Sequence' (the sequence name) rather than the target's name 'New Target', and the Session Report labels the group 'Untargeted' - so the breakdown is wrong on both axes, not just the filter. Severity corrected to P2 rather than P1: the frames are physically taken through whatever slot the wheel is parked on and the run is not damaged; the harm is downstream matching/attribution ambiguity, the same class as the NULL-metadata finding above and arguably a duplicate of its root cause on the DB side (both stem from the sequencer capture path inventing its own metadata rather than reading back what the capture actually used).

verdicts.title: The Builder tree shows a different instruction ORDER than the one that executes (drag-reorder mutates the model but never repaints)
verdicts.location_wrong: unit says 'screen:sequencer/sequencer_screen.dart' for a repaint bug that does not exist. The real (much smaller) defect is in the semantics/a11y ordering of the instruction list, not in its painting.
verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced the divergence the finding describes and then found the divergence is between the EXECUTOR and the ACCESSIBILITY TREE, not between the executor and the screen - i.e. the symptom is a harness artifact, and the stated cause ('mutates the model but never repaints') is wrong. Method: built Sequence = [Slew to Target(custom RA 17h/Dec+30), Unpark Mount, Take Exposures 4x3s] and dragged rows with synthetic press-move-release. Drops onto a card body are rejected (nothing moves anywhere); drops onto the dashed 'Insert here' zone are accepted. After an accepted drop of Take Exposures to the head of the list, `tree` still enumerated Slew / Unpark / Take Exposures, and run 3's executor logged 'Child 0: Take Exposures, Child 1: Slew to Target, Child 2: Unpark Mount' and ran it in that order - which is exactly the finding's evidence and looks damning. But a SCREENSHOT taken at the same time (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vseqrun-37.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vseqrun-38.png) shows the visible builder list already in the new order, Take Exposures first. I then made it unambiguous: dragged Take Exposures down one slot, screenshotted 1.5s after mouseup (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vseqrun-41.png) - the painted list reads Slew to Target, Take Exposures, Unpark Mount, i.e. it repainted immediately - while `tree` at that same moment still read Slew / Unpark / Take Exposures. Run 4's executor then logged 'Child 0: Slew to Target, Child 1: Take Exposures, Child 2: Unpark Mount'. So executor order == painted order != AT-SPI order. The AT-SPI child enumeration keeps the pre-drag creation order and never re-sorts; that IS a real defect, but it is an accessibility one (a screen-reader user hears the wrong order) worth P3, not the P1 'the screen lies about what will run'. Also worth flagging for whoever reads the original: its only screenshot evidence, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rseq-80.png, has 10:50:45 on the app clock, while its own log citation for the drag+run is 10:54-10:57 - so that image is the PRE-drag state and never showed a stale post-drag view at all.

verdicts.title: Light frames are written with NO pointing at all - no RA/DEC/OBJCTRA/OBJECT card and NULL mount_ra/mount_dec - after a successful slew to explicit coordinates
verdicts.duplicate_of: Overlaps the 'captured_images has NO gain/offset/sensor temp/mount pointing...' finding on the DB side (mount_ra/mount_dec/target_id NULL is the same missing-column defect in insertSequenceFrame). The FITS-header half - no RA/DEC/OBJCTRA/OBJCTDEC/OBJECT card when there is no Target group - is genuinely additional and is the part worth fixing separately.
verdicts.location_wrong: unit 'seq-node:ExposureNode' is approximately right for the FITS half (the header is assembled on the Rust capture path from the sequence context); the DB half belongs to images_dao.dart insertSequenceFrame + event_operations.dart, not to the node.
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on my own profile. Sequence with NO Target group: Slew to Target with 'Use Target Coordinates' OFF and RA 17.0000 h / Dec 30.0000 deg, then Take Exposures 4x3s LIGHT. Log: 'Slewing to RA: 17.0000h, Dec: 30.0000', 'Slewing mount sim_mount_1 to RA=17.0000h Dec=30.0000', then "Child 'Slew to Target' completed with status: Success" before the exposures started. The four resulting files (untargeted_nofilter_0001..0004.fits) have exactly 22 header cards: SIMPLE, BITPIX, NAXIS, NAXIS1/2, BZERO, BSCALE, EXPTIME, DATE-OBS, IMAGETYP, GAIN, OFFSET, CCD-TEMP, XBINNING, YBINNING, SITELAT, SITELONG, FOCUSPOS, FOCTEMP, NS-SESID, NS-FIDX, NS-NPLN. No RA, no DEC, no OBJCTRA, no OBJCTDEC, no OBJECT, no FILTER. captured_images rows 5-8 (producing_run_id=2): mount_ra, mount_dec, target_id all NULL. Control: the earlier run of the SAME app instance with a Target group did emit RA/OBJCTRA/DEC/OBJCTDEC/OBJECT - confirming the finding's parenthetical that pointing is emitted only when a Target group exists. One correction to the framing, which matters for the fix: even in the Target-group case the RA/DEC written are the TARGET's coordinates (RA=0.0/DEC=0.0 for an unedited 'New Target'), not the mount's actual reported position - so 'every light frame carries the mount's actual RA/DEC at exposure start' is not satisfied by the working path either; the writer never reads mount pointing at all. P1 stands: a night shot through Slew-with-custom-coordinates produces frames with no recorded pointing anywhere, on disk or in the DB.

verdicts.title: 'Load Previous Setup' is inert: it restores no equipment, no sequence and writes nothing to the log - it just closes the dialog
verdicts.location_wrong: unit says 'screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart'. This dialog is packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart (the 'Load Previous Setup' label is at line 407) and its behaviour lives in packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_checker.dart:_handleStartFresh (line ~244). session_handoff_service.dart is a different feature (cross-device carry-over) and a fixer would waste a pass there.
verdicts.reasoning: The no-op is real; the 'silent' half of the finding is not, and the truth is worse. Repro: four completed sequence runs with 4 sims connected, quit, relaunch. The 'Continue Session' dialog appears showing 'New Sequence / Equipment Profile: Unknown Profile / Sequence: No Sequence / Progress 4/4 frames captured' with 'Load Previous Setup' as the primary and 'Skip' as the secondary (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vseqrun-42.png). Clicking it restores NOTHING - status bar still Camera/Mount/Guider Disconnected, Focus '---', profile chip 'My Equipment 0/0' - confirming the substance of the finding. But it is not silent: a full-width GREEN success snackbar reads 'Loaded previous setup for previous target from frame 1' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vseqrun-43.png, and the same string in the accessibility tree). So the correct characterisation is a FALSE SUCCESS claim, not a dead button - which is the cry-wolf class, and changes the fix. The finding's log evidence ('app.log has zero entries in the 70s following the click') proves nothing either way: app.log is the Rust tracing stream only - it contains no Dart-side lines at all (zero occurrences of any Dart LoggingService source such as 'QuickStart', 'SequenceExecutor' or 'ImagesDao' in 904 lines of my log or in the original agent's), so the Dart logger's 'Starting fresh with context:' line could never have appeared there. Mechanism, from the code plus the DB: _handleStartFresh only acts when context.profileId / context.sequenceId are non-null and applies context.equipmentSnapshot; all four of my imaging_sessions rows have profile_id NULL, sequence_id NULL and an empty equipment_snapshot, so there is genuinely nothing to restore - the dialog already says so ('Unknown Profile', 'No Sequence') and then offers the action anyway and reports it succeeded. Two defensible fixes: disable the primary (or relabel it) when the snapshot is empty, and/or stamp profile_id/sequence_id/equipment_snapshot onto imaging_sessions so there is something to restore. P2 not P1: no data is lost and the user can reconnect manually; the damage is a false claim of restoration.
